docs.title: Welcome to the Popcorn Guineapig Detekt Rule documentation! 👋
docs.text:
The goal of this Detekt plugin is to enforce architectural rules within your Kotlin project. Define your architecture guidelines through configuration, and the plugin will automatically analyze your codebase to verify compliance, helping you maintain a consistent and well-structured architecture as your project evolves.

Take a look at our repository.

docs.title: 1. Define rules
docs.text:
Create your configuration file at the same level of your detekt.yml definition (e.g., config/detekt/popcorngp-config.json).

{
  "packagePrefix": "com.gabrielbmoro.moviedb",
  "rules": [
    {
      "filePattern": "^.*/domain/model/.+\\.kt$",
      "exclusiveDependencies": [
        "^.*/domain/model/.+\\.kt$"
      ]
    },
    {
      "filePattern": "^.*/.+Controller\\.kt$",
      "dependenciesAllowed": false
    }
  ]
}

In this first rule, I am defining that any file located under the domain/model package may only depend on other classes within the same domain/model package. This ensures that domain models remain isolated and do not introduce dependencies on other layers or modules of the application.

In the second rule, I am telling Popcorngp that any class whose name ends with *Controller.kt must not have dependencies on other internal project classes. This helps ensure that controllers remain isolated and do not become tightly coupled to other parts of the codebase.

docs.title: 2. Installing Popcorngp in your project
docs.text: This custom Detekt plugin can be used in two different ways, depending on how you run Detekt in your project.

docs.title: Option 1: Gradle integration
docs.text:
If your project uses the Detekt Gradle plugin, you can add this plugin as a detektPlugins dependency. Once configured, the custom rules will automatically be loaded and executed whenever Detekt runs as part of your Gradle build.

plugins {
    id("io.gitlab.arturbosch.detekt")
}

detekt {
    buildUponDefaultConfig = true

    config.setFrom(
        "$rootDir/config/detekt/detekt.yml"
    )
}

dependencies {
    detektPlugins("io.github.codandotv:popcornguineapig-detekt-rule:<version>)
}

This approach is recommended for most Kotlin projects because it integrates seamlessly with your existing build process and CI/CD pipelines.

docs.title: Option 2: Detekt CLI
docs.text:
If you use Detekt through the command-line interface, you can load the plugin by providing the generated JAR file using the –plugins option.

This approach is useful when running Detekt outside of Gradle or when integrating Detekt into custom tooling and scripts.

Example:

detekt \
  --input src \
  --config detekt.yml \
  --plugins popcornguineapig-detekt-rule.jar

In both cases, the plugin will discover and execute your custom architectural rules, reporting any violations according to the configuration defined in your Detekt settings.

–

Any problems you are facing, any suggestions you want to add, please feel free to reach us out.

docs.title: Existing Rules
docs.text: Popcornguineapig-detekt-rule provides a single configurable rule that enforces custom architectural dependency constraints in your Kotlin projects.

docs.title: ArchitectureRulesRule
docs.text:
Property Value Rule ID ArchitectureRulesRule Severity CodeSmell Debt 5 minutes Description Define dependency rules for your project

This rule inspects every Kotlin file in your project and checks its internal imports (imports matching the configured packagePrefix) against the rules you define in the JSON configuration file.

docs.title: Evaluation Order
docs.text:
For a given file matching a rule’s filePattern, the checks are evaluated in the following order. Only the first matching condition is applied:

  1. dependenciesAllowed — if set to false, any internal import is reported as a violation.
  2. forbiddenDependencies — if non-empty, any internal import matching one of the forbidden regex patterns is reported as a violation.
  3. exclusiveDependencies — if non-empty, any internal import that does not match any of the exclusive regex patterns is reported as a violation.
  4. If none of the conditions above are triggered (e.g., all fields are null or empty), no violation is reported.

docs.title: Rule Configuration Fields
docs.text:
Each rule entry in the rules array supports the following fields:

Field Type Description filePattern String Regex pattern matching the file paths this rule applies to. dependenciesAllowed Boolean? When set to false, the matched file is not allowed to have any internal imports. forbiddenDependencies String[] Regex patterns of packages that the file must not depend on. exclusiveDependencies String[] Regex patterns. The file may only depend on packages matching at least one of these patterns.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
No dependencies allowed — files matching *Controller.kt must have zero internal imports:

{
  "filePattern": "^.*/.+Controller\\.kt$",
  "dependenciesAllowed": false
}

Exclusive dependencies — files under domain/model may only depend on other files in domain/model:

{
  "filePattern": "^.*/domain/model/.+\\.kt$",
  "exclusiveDependencies": [
    "^.*/domain/model/.+\\.kt$"
  ]
}

Forbidden dependencies — files under data must not depend on presentation:

{
  "filePattern": "^.*/data/.+\\.kt$",
  "forbiddenDependencies": [
    "^.*/presentation/.+\\.kt$"
  ]
}

docs.title: RuleSet
docs.text:
This rule is registered under the rule set ID popcorn_guineapig_rules and referenced from your detekt.yml as:

popcorn_guineapig_rules:
  config: "config/detekt/popcorngp-config.json"

docs.title: Contributions 🤝
docs.text:
We encourage contributions of all types! Whether it’s reporting issues, suggesting new features, or submitting pull requests, you’re welcome to help improve the plugin.

  • Check out the issues page for ideas.

  • Feel free to submit pull requests.

docs.title: 1. Fork the repository
docs.text: Create a fork of the repository in your own GitHub account.

docs.title: 5. Commit the changes to your fork
docs.text:
git checkout -b "your-branch-name"
git add .
git commit -m "Describe your changes"
git push

docs.title: 6. Create your Pull Request
docs.text:
• Create a new Pull Request, selecting the original repository as the base and your branch as the compare branch

  • Provide a clear title and a detailed description of your changes

  • Submit the PR and wait for review and possible approval.

🤗 Happy coding!
